parts.text: Fig. 2.1 shows a train. Fig. 2.1 The total mass of the train and its passengers is 750 000 kg. The train is travelling at a speed of 84 m / s. The driver applies the brakes and the train takes 80 s to slow down to a speed of 42 m / s.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Calculate the impulse applied to the train as it slows down. impulse = ......................................................... [3]

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text:
impulse OR Δp = m(v – u) in any form
(impulse =) 750 000 (84 – 42)
(impulse =) 3.2 × 10 N s or m kg / s
7

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Calculate the average resultant force applied to the train as it slows down. force = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 2(b)
ms.text:
Ft = impulse OR Δp in any form
OR (F =) (impulse OR Δp) / t
(F = 3.2 x 10 / 80 =) 3.9 ×10 N
7
5

ms.label: 2(c)
ms.text: reduces drag / air resistance (experienced by the train) / more streamlined

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text: less drag / air resistance (at slower speeds)

ms.label: 2(e)
ms.text: (maximum) friction (force) between rails and train reduced / train may slide
